def capture(
    root: Path | str,
    body: str,
    *,
    source_kind: str = "user_instruction",
    work: str | None = None,
    amends: str | None = None,
    force: bool = False,
    transport_transform: str = "none",
    newline_normalization: str = "none",
) -> dict:
    """Capture an authoritative source VERBATIM before any interpretation.

    Idempotent: an exact canonical digest returns the existing receipt
    (duplicate=true) and never creates a second one. Body is written first,
    then metadata, then the index -- so a crash after the body leaves a
    detectable orphan that recovery can reconcile, and a crash before any
    durable write loses nothing.
    """
    root = Path(root)
    if not isinstance(body, str) or not body:
        return {"ok": False, "code": "INVALID_SOURCE", "detail": "empty source body"}
    # CORE-001: the received UTF-8 body IS the authority. Credential masking is
    # a display/export concern and must never run before the canonical digest,
    # dedupe or persistence -- masking before identity made two byte-distinct
    # sources collapse onto one receipt (SOURCES.md:38-44).
    detected_sensitive = _looks_sensitive(body)
    sensitive = detected_sensitive
    body_bytes = body.encode("utf-8")

    if len(body_bytes) > _BODY_MAX:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
            "detail": f"source body exceeds {_BODY_MAX} byte limit",
        }
    if source_kind not in SOURCE_KINDS:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
            "detail": f"unknown source kind {source_kind!r}",
        }
    if work is not None and not re.fullmatch(r"T-\d+", work):
        return {"ok": False, "code": "INVALID_ID", "detail": f"work {work!r}"}

        # USER_INTERRUPT provenance: `user_explicit: true` marks a ticket that
        # was born from an explicit user request (with a durable intake
        # receipt in `source_receipts`), so the scheduler can rank it above
        # speculative/planned work without reading prose.
        "user_explicit",
        # Implementation-delta evidence: `implementation_delta: none` records
        # that BUILD produced no attributable diff for this ticket (the
        # implementation already existed / was inherited), so closure must not
        # be forced to manufacture one. `implementation_source` names the
        # receipt/event the inherited implementation came from when known.
        "implementation_delta",
        "implementation_source",
    }
)


# The closed closure-mode vocabulary (orchestration repair, CORE). A DONE
# ticket may carry exactly one of these; anything else fails closed in the
# validator rather than being read as unspecified.
CLOSURE_MODES = ("own_patch", "inherited_verified", "cohort")

# The closed blocker-scope vocabulary. `ticket` (default) means only this
# ticket is stuck; `goal` means no safe useful work toward the current goal
# can continue without an external/operator dependency.
BLOCKER_SCOPES = ("ticket", "goal")

# The closed implementation-delta vocabulary.
IMPLEMENTATION_DELTAS = ("none",)


def closure_modes() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The closed closure-mode set (own_patch | inherited_verified | cohort)."""
    return CLOSURE_MODES


def blocker_scopes() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The closed blocker-scope set (ticket | goal)."""
    return BLOCKER_SCOPES


def ticket_blocker_scope(ticket: dict) -> str | None:
    """The normalized blocker scope of a ticket, or None when absent/invalid.

    Legacy tickets carry no scope -> None (conservatively treated as ticket).
    An unparsable value is never silently read as goal: fail closed to None.
    """
    value = str(((ticket or {}).get("fields") or {}).get("blocker_scope") or "").strip().lower()
    if value in BLOCKER_SCOPES:
        return value
    return None


def is_goal_blocked_ticket(ticket: dict) -> bool:
    """True when this ## BLOCKED ticket declares goal scope."""
    return ticket.get("section") == "## BLOCKED" and ticket_blocker_scope(ticket) == "goal"


def is_user_explicit(ticket: dict) -> bool:
    """True when the ticket is stamped as born from an explicit user request.

    `user_explicit: true` is the ONLY value that arms the scheduler signal --
    anything else (absent, false, typo) is not explicit, so a misspelled flag
    can never silently outrank planned work.
    """
    return str(((ticket or {}).get("fields") or {}).get("user_explicit") or "").strip().lower() == "true"


def ticket_closure_mode(ticket: dict) -> str | None:
    """The normalized closure mode of a ticket, or None when absent/invalid.

    Legacy/unspecified tickets carry no mode. An unrecognized value is None
    (never read as a mode it is not) -- the validator is the gate that
    rejects an unrecognized spelling on a NEW-format closure.
    """
    value = str(((ticket or {}).get("fields") or {}).get("closure_mode") or "").strip().lower()
    if value in CLOSURE_MODES:
        return value
    return None

@_state_guard
def ticket_move(
    project_root: Path | str,
    action: str,
    ticket_id: str,
    agent: str,
    payload: str = "",
    dry_run: bool = False,
    scope: str = "ticket",
) -> Result:
    """Move a ticket between BOARD sections.

    `done` is NOT a section move: it is the atomic ticket-closure operation
    (NITRO dogfood III, T-591). A standalone `done` here would leave the split
    (BOARD DONE[x] while STATE still names the ticket in a ticket-bearing
    phase) that the composition audit reproduced. `done` delegates to
    finish_ticket so one public operation, one lifecycle meaning.

    `block` accepts an optional blocker `scope` (ticket | goal, default
    ticket): a goal-scope block declares that no independent work toward the
    current goal can progress, which is the ONLY blocker form allowed to stop
    the autonomous loop (orchestration repair).
    """
    if action == "done":
        return finish_ticket(project_root, ticket_id, agent, dry_run=dry_run)
    root = Path(project_root)
    now, utc = _now(), _utc_iso()
    plan = _ticket_targets(root, action, ticket_id, agent, payload, now, utc, scope=scope)
    if isinstance(plan, Result):
        return plan
    if dry_run:
        return _render_plan(plan)
    return apply_plan(root, plan)

@_state_guard
def user_request(
    project_root: Path | str,
    agent: str,
    body: str,
    priority: str = "P2",
    verify: str = "",
    needs: list[str] | None = None,
    dry_run: bool = False,
) -> Result:
    """The canonical USER_INTERRUPT operation (orchestration repair).

    Ordering is the CORE contract for explicit user intent:

      1. CAPTURE the raw request as a durable intake receipt (verbatim,
         idempotent -- an identical request returns the existing receipt);
      2. PROJECT it onto the board as a `user_explicit: true` ticket linked
         to that receipt;
      3. leave the active ticket's execution state UNTOUCHED -- persist
         immediately, execute when safe (the router ranks the new ticket
         ahead of planned work at the next START decision, and `saipen
         continue` re-picks after any block).

    A crash between (1) and (2) leaves an ORPHAN_USER_INTENT (receipt without
    board projection), which the audit finding detects and `saipen source
    recover` reconciles -- the request itself is never lost to agent memory.
    """
    root = Path(project_root)
    if not body or not body.strip():
        return _refuse("INVALID_SOURCE", "user request body is required")
    from . import intake

    captured = intake.capture(
        root,
        body,
        source_kind="user_instruction",
    )
    if not captured.get("ok"):
        return _refuse(
            captured.get("code", "SOURCE_CAPTURE_FAILED"),
            f"user request could not be captured durably: {captured.get('detail', '')}",
        )
    receipt_id = captured.get("receipt")
    # Persist the receipt BEFORE any board work; the ticket projection is a
    # separate journaled transaction so a failure to project never loses the
    # user's request (crash window A, orchestration repair).
    description = body.strip()
    # A multi-line request is projected as its first line with the full body
    # staying authoritative in the receipt (one ticket_add renders exactly one
    # board line).
    description = description.splitlines()[0].strip() or "user request"
    if len(description) > 160:
        description = description[:157].rstrip() + "..."
    result = ticket_add(
        root,
        agent,
        priority,
        description,
        list(needs or []),
        verify or "verify the requested behavior end-to-end",
        dry_run=dry_run,
        user_explicit=True,
        receipt_id=receipt_id,
    )
    if isinstance(result, Result) and not result.ok:
        result.data = dict(result.data or {})
        result.data["receipt"] = receipt_id
        return result
    return result

"""Engine exceptions and the closed set of stable result codes.

A weak model should reason about a CODE, not parse an essay. REGISTRY.json owns
the closed set; OPS.md documents result shape without becoming a second list.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .registry import load_registry, require_string_list

CODES = frozenset(require_string_list(load_registry(), "error_codes"))


class EngineError(Exception):
    """Base for every engine refusal.

    Carries a `code` from `CODES` and, where one exists, the exact executable
    next action. "operation failed" tells a cold weak model nothing; the point
    of this class is that it cannot be raised without naming which refusal it
    is.
    """

    code = "VALIDATION_FAILED"

    def __init__(
        self, message: str, *, code: str | None = None, next_action: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        if code is not None:
            self.code = code
        if self.code not in CODES:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.code!r} is not one of OPS.md's stable result codes")
        self.message = message
        self.next_action = next_action

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        tail = f"\nrun: {self.next_action}" if self.next_action else ""
        return f"REFUSE [{self.code}] {self.message}{tail}"


class ParseError(EngineError):
    """A canonical file does not match the shape CORE section 1.2 fixes.

    Raised BEFORE any mutation: a malformed BOARD/STATE/LOG must refuse rather
    than be half-understood and half-rewritten.
    """

    code = "VALIDATION_FAILED"


class StaleSnapshotError(EngineError):
    """A plan computed against one snapshot met a different one at apply time.

    Optimistic concurrency, sequential edition: the operation is refused, not
    retried silently, because the decision that produced it was made against
    state that no longer exists.
    """

    code = "STALE_STATE"

@_state_guard
def finish_ticket(
    project_root: Path | str,
    ticket_id: str,
    agent: str,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    digest_text: str | None = None,
    digest_done: str | None = None,
    digest_awaiting: str | None = None,
    prefix_run: str | None = None,
) -> Result:
    """Atomically finish a ticket: LOG + BOARD + STATE in ONE journaled plan.
    The public `ticket done` semantics become this operation.

    The release closure passes `digest_text` so the human digest commits in
    the SAME journaled transaction as the ticket closure (T-994 / § 16), and
    `prefix_run` to emit its ONE truthful release RUN event through the same
    canonical LOG builder (§ 15). The `digest_done` / `digest_awaiting` hints
    are reserved for the no-publish digest shape.
    """
    root = Path(project_root)
    now, utc = _now(), _utc_iso()
    plan = _plan_finish_ticket(
        root,
        ticket_id,
        agent,
        now,
        utc,
        digest_text=digest_text,
        digest_done=digest_done,
        digest_awaiting=digest_awaiting,
        prefix_run=prefix_run,
    )
    if isinstance(plan, Result):
        return plan
    if dry_run:
        return _render_plan(plan)
    return apply_plan(root, plan)

@_state_guard
def finish_ticket(
    project_root: Path | str,
    ticket_id: str,
    agent: str,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    digest_text: str | None = None,
    digest_done: str | None = None,
    digest_awaiting: str | None = None,
    prefix_run: str | None = None,
    closure_mode: str = "own_patch",
    closure_cohort: str | None = None,
) -> Result:
    """Atomically finish a ticket: LOG + BOARD + STATE in ONE journaled plan.
    The public `ticket done` semantics become this operation.

    The release closure passes `digest_text` so the human digest commits in
    the SAME journaled transaction as the ticket closure (T-994 / § 16), and
    `prefix_run` to emit its ONE truthful release RUN event through the same
    canonical LOG builder (§ 15). The `digest_done` / `digest_awaiting` hints
    are reserved for the no-publish digest shape.

    `closure_mode` (own_patch | inherited_verified | cohort, default
    own_patch) records HOW the ticket satisfied its intent (orchestration
    repair): own_patch closes on an attributable implementation diff,
    inherited_verified closes a verification-only ticket whose implementation
    already existed in the worktree (no new code, no fake commit), and cohort
    closes a ticket that ships inside a C-### batch with its peers. Every mode
    still requires this ticket's own verification evidence -- evidence closure
    is separate from repository publication.
    """
    root = Path(project_root)
    now, utc = _now(), _utc_iso()
    plan = _plan_finish_ticket(
        root,
        ticket_id,
        agent,
        now,
        utc,
        digest_text=digest_text,
        digest_done=digest_done,
        digest_awaiting=digest_awaiting,
        prefix_run=prefix_run,
        closure_mode=closure_mode,
        closure_cohort=closure_cohort,
    )
    if isinstance(plan, Result):
        return plan
    if dry_run:
        return _render_plan(plan)
    return apply_plan(root, plan)

replacements.newString:
## Orchestration Repair: Workable Scheduling and Evidence-Based Closure (T-1302)

Motivating failure (the FastPrompter class): a ticket at REVIEW/SHIP whose implementation already existed in a shared dirty worktree could not isolate an exact per-ticket diff, the ticket blocked, the scheduler then selected an unworkable release whose gates were blocked, and the loop stopped -- while a fresh explicit user request sat unpersisted because completion of the old ticket came first. The dirty-tree safety rules (never revert, never commit unowned work, fail closed on unknown ownership) are unchanged; the orchestration model around them changed.

- **User intent persists first.** A new explicit user request is persisted immediately (intake receipt + BOARD ticket marked `user_explicit: true`) BEFORE any unrelated active-ticket completion work. `saipen user-request <text>` is the canonical entry; `saipen ticket add --user` marks a ticket manually. Persist immediately, execute at a safe boundary -- never "finish the old ticket first, maybe persist later".
- **Ticket block is not a goal block.** A `## BLOCKED` ticket carries `blocker_scope: ticket` (this task cannot progress; independent work may continue) or `blocker_scope: goal` (no safe work remains without an external/operator dependency). Only goal scope stops the loop, and the scheduler re-picks after every block/unblock/finish/interrupt transition.
- **`next_action` is the next WORKABLE action.** A ticket is workable only when status allows execution, every `needs:` dependency is DONE (a blocked dependency is not DONE), no operator gate precedes it, and it is not a release whose gates are red. A release ticket whose required tickets are BLOCKED is never selected while an independent workable ticket exists. `state.stop_reason: GOAL_BLOCKED` records a legitimate global stop; the validator rejects it whenever a workable ticket exists.
- **Closure is separate from Git publication.** A ticket's SHIP/DONE means implementation intent satisfied with evidence and provenance recorded -- not that a per-ticket commit exists. `closure_mode` on the DONE line records the provenance: `own_patch` (attributable implementation diff), `inherited_verified` (no new implementation added; this agent verified/reviewed only -- valid when BUILD produced no diff), or `cohort` (membership in a C-### closure cohort whose overlapping files ship together; `closure_cohort: C-###` required, publication deferred to the cohort's release). `implementation_delta: none` records that BUILD produced no code change.
- **Overlapping-worktree example.** T-A, T-B, T-C all modify `main.py`; T-A's exact diff cannot be isolated after accumulation. T-A reaches VERIFY/REVIEW with no new code from the current agent: close it `closure_mode: inherited_verified` with its verification evidence, or `closure_mode: cohort, closure_cohort: C-014` when the verified changes ship as a batch. Never commit unowned work, never fabricate hunk ownership -- unknown ownership stays unknown.

## Guarantees, Bounds, and Non-Claims
Stated plainly, at the strength the implementation actually supports.

# Changelog

## 8.1.0 -- 2026-09-08 -- Workable Scheduling and Evidence-Based Closure (T-1302)

A real production failure exposed a core orchestration flaw: a ticket at REVIEW/SHIP whose implementation already existed in a shared dirty worktree could not isolate an exact per-ticket diff, the ticket blocked, the scheduler then selected an unworkable release whose gates were blocked, and the loop stopped -- while a fresh explicit user request sat unpersisted. The dirty-tree safety rules are unchanged; the orchestration model around them changed.

- Explicit user intents persist before active-ticket completion: new `saipen user-request` command (and `ticket add --user`) writes the intake receipt + a `user_explicit: true` BOARD ticket immediately, and the scheduler routes new explicit workable requests ahead of planned/improve work.
- Blocked tickets no longer halt independent work: `## BLOCKED` tickets carry `blocker_scope: ticket|goal`; only goal scope stops the loop. The router re-picks after every block/unblock/finish and emits `stop_reason: GOAL_BLOCKED` only when no workable ticket remains (persisted in STATE).
- `next_action` is dependency/workability aware: a release ticket whose required tickets are blocked is never selected while an independent workable ticket exists; the validator fails unworkable picks, blocked phases with workable tickets, and GOAL_BLOCKED stop reasons that are false.
- Verification-only / inherited / cohort closure: `ticket done --closure-mode inherited_verified|cohort [--closure-cohort C-###]` closes a ticket without an artificial per-ticket commit when BUILD produced no diff (`implementation_delta: none`), and COHORT closure defers publication to a C-### cohort of overlapping files. Ticket SHIP is separated from Git/release publication.
- Validator + audit surface: two new hard fail sites (false global block, inherited closure without verification evidence) with red controls (324 -> 326), a cohort-dangling WARN slug, and board.schema.json accepts the new optional fields while old projects load unchanged.
- Verification: focused orchestration-repair suite + existing core suites green, validator 0 FAIL on the live repository, ruff clean.

closure, USER_INTERRUPT persistence, ticket vs goal block, GOAL_BLOCKED stop.

exact patch isolation, the scheduler then selected an unworkable release whose
gates were blocked, and the loop stopped while a fresh explicit user request sat
unpersisted. Every test here drives canonical operations only -- no hand-editing
of the project files to force a result.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import json
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

TOOLS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
if str(TOOLS) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))

from saipen_engine.board import is_user_explicit, parse_board, ticket_is_workable  # noqa: E402
from saipen_engine.journal import ensure_project_lineage  # noqa: E402
from saipen_engine.operations import (  # noqa: E402
    finish_ticket,
    ticket_add,
    ticket_move,
    user_request,
)
from saipen_engine.router import route_next  # noqa: E402
from saipen_engine.state import parse_state  # noqa: E402


class OrchestrationFixture(unittest.TestCase):
    def make_project(self, *, active: bool = False, phase: str = "DONE") -> Path:
        base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="saipen-orchestration-"))
        self.addCleanup(lambda: shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True))
        project = base / "project"
        (project / ".saipen").mkdir(parents=True)
        now = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        task = "T-7" if active else "none"
        next_action = "PHASE BUILD T-7" if active else "saipen continue"
        transition_from = "SCOUT" if active else "DONE"
        (project / ".saipen" / "STATE.md").write_text(
            "---\n"
            f"phase: {phase}\n"
            f"task: {task}\n"
            f'next_action: "{next_action}"\n'
            'blocker: ""\n'
            f"transition_from: {transition_from}\n"
            "saipen_version: 7\n"
            "schema_version: 3\n"
            "last_event: 1\n"
            "style_contract: ded-4ae736e4\n"
            f'saipen_home: "{str(TOOLS).replace(chr(92), chr(92) * 2)}"\n'
            "agent: tester\n"
            "requires:\n  - filesystem\n  - python\n"
            "mode: full\n"
            f'updated: "{now}"\n'
            "---\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        doing = (
            f"- [/] T-7 [P1] Existing Work | verify: existing proof | "
            f"owner: tester | claim_time: {now}\n"
            if active
            else ""
        )
        (project / ".saipen" / "BOARD.md").write_text(
            f"## DOING\n{doing}## TODO\n## DONE\n## BLOCKED\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        ticket = " [T-7]" if active else ""
        (project / ".saipen" / "LOG.md").write_text(
            f"- 24.08.26 00:00 [E-001]{ticket} [agent: tester] RUN: fixture -> PASS\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        ensure_project_lineage(project)
        return project

    def state(self, project: Path) -> dict:
        return parse_state((project / ".saipen" / "STATE.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def board(self, project: Path) -> dict:
        return parse_board((project / ".saipen" / "BOARD.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def route(self, project: Path) -> dict:
        return route_next(
            (project / ".saipen" / "STATE.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
            (project / ".saipen" / "BOARD.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
            current_agent="tester",
        )

    def add(
        self,
        project: Path,
        description: str,
        *,
        priority: str = "P1",
        needs: list[str] | None = None,

    ) -> str:
        result = ticket_add(
            project,
            "tester",
            priority,
            description,
            needs or [],
            verify,
        )
        self.assertTrue(result.ok, result.to_dict())
        return result.data["ticket"]

+## Orchestration Repair: Workable Scheduling and Evidence-Based Closure (T-1302)
+
+Motivating failure (the FastPrompter class): a ticket at REVIEW/SHIP whose implementation already existed in a shared dirty worktree could not isolate an exact per-ticket diff, the ticket blocked, the scheduler then selected an unworkable release whose gates were blocked, and the loop stopped -- while a fresh explicit user request sat unpersisted because completion of the old ticket came first. The dirty-tree safety rules (never revert, never commit unowned work, fail closed on unknown ownership) are unchanged; the orchestration model around them changed.
+
+- **User intent persists first.** A new explicit user request is persisted immediately (intake receipt + BOARD ticket marked `user_explicit: true`) BEFORE any unrelated active-ticket completion work. `saipen user-request <text>` is the canonical entry; `saipen ticket add --user` marks a ticket manually. Persist immediately, execute at a safe boundary -- never "finish the old ticket first, maybe persist later".
+- **Ticket block is not a goal block.** A `## BLOCKED` ticket carries `blocker_scope: ticket` (this task cannot progress; independent work may continue) or `blocker_scope: goal` (no safe work remains without an external/operator dependency). Only goal scope stops the loop, and the scheduler re-picks after every block/unblock/finish/interrupt transition.
+- **`next_action` is the next WORKABLE action.** A ticket is workable only when status allows execution, every `needs:` dependency is DONE (a blocked dependency is not DONE), no operator gate precedes it, and it is not a release whose gates are red. A release ticket whose required tickets are BLOCKED is never selected while an independent workable ticket exists. `state.stop_reason: GOAL_BLOCKED` records a legitimate global stop; the validator rejects it whenever a workable ticket exists.
+- **Closure is separate from Git publication.** A ticket's SHIP/DONE means implementation intent satisfied with evidence and provenance recorded -- not that a per-ticket commit exists. `closure_mode` on the DONE line records the provenance: `own_patch` (attributable implementation diff), `inherited_verified` (no new implementation added; this agent verified/reviewed only -- valid when BUILD produced no diff), or `cohort` (membership in a C-### closure cohort whose overlapping files ship together; `closure_cohort: C-###` required, publication deferred to the cohort's release). `implementation_delta: none` records that BUILD produced no code change.
+- **Overlapping-worktree example.** T-A, T-B, T-C all modify `main.py`; T-A's exact diff cannot be isolated after accumulation. T-A reaches VERIFY/REVIEW with no new code from the current agent: close it `closure_mode: inherited_verified` with its verification evidence, or `closure_mode: cohort, closure_cohort: C-014` when the verified changes ship as a batch. Never commit unowned work, never fabricate hunk ownership -- unknown ownership stays unknown.
